Package com.csse3200.game.win

Class BossRoster

java.lang.Object
com.csse3200.game.win.BossRoster
public final class BossRoster extends Object
The fixed list of bosses the win depends on: the final boss, and the mini bosses of the side rooms. It is data only. It says WHICH enemies matter; WinEvaluator decides what their deaths are worth.

How a boss is named. The game already saves every kill under a stable id of the form <map name>:<x>,<y>, where the tile is the enemy's marker tile in the map file (see EnemyId.of and EnemyRegistry). The roster uses exactly those ids, so a kill is known with no new component on any enemy, and it survives a save and a load. Build each id with EnemyId.of(mapName, new GridPoint2(x, y)), never by hand-typing the colon.

The roster (marker tiles are the ones in the shipped map files): 

 FINAL BOSS   Zeus                     Level 3 - Zeus's Palace : 83,5    (the map name contains an em dash)
 required     Cerberus                 Hound's Den             : 40,2
 required     Medusa                   Gorgon's Gallery        : 34,3
 required     Minotaur                 Minotaur's Labyrinth    : 37,5
 required     Minotaur                 Shades' Barracks        : 40,5
 required     Cyclops                  Cyclops Forge           : 37,3
 required     Centaur (rear)           Centaur Pavilion        : 38,5
 required     Medusa (rear)            Zeus's Outer Guard      : 41,3
 required     Zeus                     Zeus's Thunder Hall     : 38,3
 escort       Centaur                  Minotaur's Labyrinth    : 27,5
 escort       Centaur (front)          Centaur Pavilion        : 26,5
 escort       Cyclops                  Zeus's Outer Guard      : 30,3

"Required" means the boss that guards the end of the room, which is the rightmost boss in it. An "escort" is another boss-type enemy in the same room. Escorts are listed so the win screen can show them, but they are NOT needed for WinTier.GLORY.

Limitations: an id is a map name plus a tile, so renaming a map or moving a boss marker silently breaks the roster for existing saves. BossRosterMapsTest reads the real map files and fails the moment the roster and the maps disagree. The Zeus in Level 2 and the Zeus in the Thunder Hall are NOT the final boss; only the one in Level 3 ends the game.

Style reference: EnemyId (a small utility class with a private constructor).
